title: Omarchy: the computer an agent can read
thesis: Omarchy is an Arch, Hyprland and Quickshell distribution by DHH designed so a coding agent can read and change the whole system: settings are text files and commands, the desktop is plugins, crashes go to your agent; Quattro adds packages, an update guard, snapshots and app isolation to keep that safe, and the cost is trust in unsandboxed plugins, unattended agents, a single shell process and Arch's churn.
one_idea: An agent can only change what it can read; Omarchy puts most of the computer in reach of one.
end_line: An agent can only change what it can read.

youtube.title: Omarchy explained: the Linux setup built for AI agents
youtube.summary: Omarchy is David Heinemeier Hansson's Linux distribution, built on Arch, Hyprland and Quickshell, and designed so a coding agent can read and change most of the system: text files, a command line and a desktop made of plugins. Its creator says the Quattro release was almost exclusively built by agents. This video explains what Omarchy is, why plain text files and commands make a system agent-friendly, how crashes and plugins work, the guard rails that keep it from breaking, and what the freedom costs you.
youtube.pinned_comment: Every claim in this video is sourced; the sources are in the description. Two things we checked and corrected from earlier coverage: the repository now lives at github.com/omacom/omarchy, and Steam and the Windows VM are installed from the Omarchy menu rather than preinstalled. If you spot a factual error, reply here and we will pin the correction.

shots.headline: Built almost entirely by agents
shots.say: In September 2026, David Heinemeier Hansson wrote an unusual sentence about his Linux system. Omarchy Quattro has almost exclusively been built by agents.

visual.highlight: In fact, Omarchy Quattro has almost exclusively been built by agents.

shots.headline: What an agent does
shots.say: Agents here means AI coding assistants. They read files, run commands and change a system on their own.

shots.headline: Popular, for a Linux setup
shots.say: Its GitHub repository has more than 45,000 stars. The project counts about 1.3 million ISO downloads in its first year.
shots.credit: Sources: GitHub API and omarchy.org, read 2026-10-20

shots.say: First, what is Omarchy? It is not an operating system written from scratch.

shots.headline: Arch, Hyprland, Quickshell
shots.say: The manual names the three main layers: Arch Linux, the window manager Hyprland, and Quickshell.

visual.highlight: Omarchy is an omakase Linux distribution based on Arch, the tiling window manager Hyprland, and the desktop construction-kit Quickshell.

shots.headline: Tiling: no overlapping windows
shots.say: Above it is Hyprland, a tiling window manager. By default, tiled windows don't overlap. Each new window takes a share of the screen.

shots.headline: What a compositor does
shots.say: Hyprland calls itself a dynamic tiling Wayland compositor. A compositor puts every app's window on screen. Wayland is the newer protocol for that, replacing X11.

the compositor"] B[Browser] --> C E[Editor] --> C C --> S[Screen]

shots.chapter: Why build a computer for an agent?
shots.say: So why design a computer for an AI agent?

visual.text: Why build a computer for an *agent*?

shots.headline: Text in, text out
shots.say: Start with what a coding agent is good at. It reads text, writes text, runs a command, and checks what happened.

shots.headline: A system you can read
shots.say: For that to work, the agent has to be able to read the system. Omarchy is configured mainly through plain text files, and its command line reaches the same tools as its menus.

shots.chapter: What does the agent actually do?
shots.say: So what does the agent actually do on this computer?

shots.headline: From crash to agent
shots.say: The clearest example is a crash. When a program crashes, Linux records it, and an Omarchy script watching the system log shows a notification.

visual.source:
graph LR
  A[App] --> B[systemd-coredump]
  B --> C[omarchy-crash-watch]
  C --> N[Notification]
  N --> G[Agent]

shots.headline: Snapshot, then update
shots.say: That command, omarchy update, takes a file-system snapshot first, then updates the packages.

graph LR
  P[pacman -Syu] -.->|stopped| X[Guard]
  O[omarchy update] --> S[Snapshot]
  S --> K[Packages]
